gates.evidence: The Store Screen and 15-second game are SFW surfaces with no sensitive topics.
Rewards +10 credits (in-app resource r1), no clicks, installs, or cash.
Gain framing ('Play a 15-second game to get +10 credits'), no dark patterns or loss framing.
User taps the pill and explicitly chooses 'Play for +10'.
Offer clearly states 'Play a 15-second game to get +10 credits. 3 per day.'
Decline option 'Not now' is available and leaves the user on s05 with no penalty.
Placed on Store Screen (s05), completely away from active chat generation.
Eligibility states: 'All users, including subscribers, on every app open', violating subscriber/payer exclusion guidelines.

scores.evidence: Triggered on Store Screen when balance is low (<30 credits), offering +10 credits. Fits the moment when users are in the store looking at credit balances.
Native placement on Store Screen, preserves app flow, and is strictly additive.
Capped at 3 per day (+30 credits), far below pack sizes, but eligibility explicitly includes subscribers, creating potential cannibalization risk.
Cost to serve per view ($0.0018) is well below net revenue per view ($0.009-0.015); reward value is appropriate.
Reaches users visiting the Store Screen with a low balance (<30 credits), which is a moderate sub-segment of DAU.
Uses SIM-RWD with button entry, SSV, and simple resource delta patch on s05.
References r1 (Credits), k1, s05 (Store Screen), and store elements correctly.
Explicitly capped at 3 per day with a 30-minute cooldown.
Defines primary metric (Refills per DAU and total revenue per user), guardrails, and a 10% user-level holdout for 4 weeks.

requiredChanges: Restrict eligibility to non-paying users and exclude subscribers/payers to prevent cannibalization and comply with payer suppression guidelines.
Consider expanding the trigger or adding an in-chat depletion trigger to capture higher intent when users hit the zero-credit wall.
parsed.topConcern: The proposal explicitly includes subscribers in its eligibility criteria ('All users, including subscribers'), violating payer/subscriber exclusion guardrails.
